report:
Reviewed all four implementation entries and the sole associated test against the complete definition_identity claim. The requirements are discovery by spelling/scope/namespace followed by symbol-based semantic references, and invariant definition identity across import renaming or alternative paths. Captured symbols-guide and architectural-foundations explain that this applies to definitions represented by the symbol family; generic parameters, locals and fields intentionally use separate scoped identities.

resolve/mod.rs resolve_path returns existing rib entries for locals/parameters/self and maps resolved definitions to Resolution::Sym. Its module and import traversal returns the target Symbol directly: a named import checks the introduced spelling then follows its target, and module/enum globs return contained symbols. Selected precedence buckets deduplicate equal symbols so repeated routes do not manufacture additional definitions or ambiguity. External named_children filters exported edge names and namespaces but constructs the canonical external handle from definition coordinates and kind, not the export spelling. The existing limitation resolving some parameter-qualified paths is about supported discovery; it is not a replacement name-based identity for successful references.

The associated ribs.rs Resolution enum keeps LocalId, GenericParam, Symbol and SelfTy distinct, and ribs select the innermost name/namespace binding without changing the stored identity. The symbol/mod.rs macro-generated family wraps the existing local tracked item or external SymExt; erasure/typed conversions reuse the inner handle. Equality/hash do not include the chosen lookup path or import alias. External interned identity contains crate/index/kind, with namespace on lookup edges. The ty.rs entry stores ADT Symbol, named/opaque TypeAliasSymbol, associated-item identity and TraitSymbol plus arguments rather than source paths. Captured downstream infer_ctx resolve_path maps a successful Resolution::Sym directly to Res::Def, and captured Typed IR PathResolution and ResolvedCallTarget store Symbol/FnSymbol. These representative consumers substantiate the intended identity boundary without claiming an exhaustive test of every semantic reference.

The only associated test, representation_spec::todo::symbols_definition_identity, has no executable assertions and explicitly defers the distinct-path/same-symbol and equal-spelling/different-scope resolution matrix. Its comment correctly rejects current output examples as sufficient evidence. Verification remains TODO: source fixtures must resolve direct, renamed-import and alternate paths and compare actual resulting identities and completed semantic references, with same-spelling definitions in distinct scopes/namespaces as controls. Existing representation and traversal inspection does not discharge those assertions or establish identity stability for arbitrary source edits beyond the stated import/path equivalence. No code changes or tests executed; commands were fresh review start/read and source inspection before record. No additional requested edits; the test deferral remains visible.
